answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to post a stake that it forfeits on provable misbehavior, so one operator spinning up thousands of identities pays for every one. Pair that with a reputation ledger that only counts endorsements from peers who have already earned standing, so new fake accounts gain nothing from vouching for each other. Bonds plus slow, earned trust make a sybil swarm expensive at the nadir of its usefulness and easy to spot in the echo of its coordinated votes.
